PROMOTION (read this first). The shadow TU verified 7/7 text-only and did emit this class's vtable, but it did so against TU-local shadow classes rather than the real header, and that is what the promotion had to replace. Which destructor variants mwccarm emits, and in what order, turns on two conditions, and an intermediate rewrite that met only one of them -- a file that declared `extern int _ZTV10daMcFlag_c[]` and so emitted no vtable of its own -- odr-used neither destructor and came back MISSING _ZN10daMcFlag_cD1Ev/_ZN10daMcFlag_cD0Ev at 5/7. The committed file is the class's KEY-FUNCTION TU: InitResources is the first declared virtual, and include/daMcFlag_c.h declares the destructor INLINE, which together make mwccarm emit D1 then D0 -- the cartridge's order, D1 at 0x02112078 and D0 at 0x021120a8, with no D2 -- plus this class's _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS. That is what the nine compiler_only_output rows below are. VPTR SPELLING: the source writes `&_ZTV10daMcFlag_c[2]`, but mwccarm folds the 8-byte address-point bias at compile time -- all three R_ARM_ABS32 relocations naming the symbol carry addend 0 over a zero content word -- so after production isolation empties the emitted section and turns the symbol into an import (SHN_UNDEF in build/src/actors/d_a_mc_flag.o), each store resolves to symbols.txt's 0x02113ba0, which IS the address point: 0x02113b98 = 0 offset-to-top, 0x02113b9c = _ZTI10daMcFlag_c, 0x02113ba0 = slot 0 (InitResources, 0x02112190).
